findings.title: Embed access control relies on the spoofable Referer header and ALLOWALL framing
findings.body: ensure_embeddable authorizes only by comparing the host of request.referer to embeddable_host. Referer is trivially forged by any non-browser client. It is also often stripped by privacy settings or Referrer-Policy, so legitimate embeds fail. The response then sets X-Frame-Options to ALLOWALL, which removes clickjacking protection for the page. A logged-in user visiting a malicious page could be framed. Because current_user is used, the framed content can include user-specific data.

findings.title: Embed URL host is never validated in the controller before enqueuing a retrieve job
findings.body: The `embed_url` param is passed to the retrieve_topic job without checking its host. Validation happens only inside the job (TopicRetriever.invalid_host?). Any request carrying the correct Referer can therefore enqueue arbitrary jobs. The controller spec expects TopicRetriever.new to be called synchronously, but the code enqueues a job, so that spec does not match the implementation.

findings.title: Referer interpolated unescaped into inline JS and used as postMessage targetOrigin
findings.body: `request.referer` is written into a JS string literal. ERB HTML-escapes it, but that is not JS escaping. A quote or backslash in the URL could break the literal. The full URL path is also not a valid targetOrigin, which must be an origin, so postMessage silently fails to deliver for any referer containing a path. As a result, the resize message never reaches the parent page.

findings.title: Origin check uses substring indexOf
findings.body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring test. An origin that happens to be a substring of discourseUrl (e.g. an empty or partial string) passes. It should be an exact origin comparison.

findings.title: import mutates the caller's string and interpolates unescaped URL into raw HTML
findings.body: `contents <<` mutates the argument in place. This also breaks on frozen strings. The sha1 is computed from the mutated content. The url is placed unescaped into an href in raw_html posts, which are not sanitized. Remote feed content is rendered as-is, creating a stored XSS risk.

findings.title: Kernel#open on a URL (SSRF / command execution)
findings.body: `open(url)` (and `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in poll_feed) uses Kernel#open. With open-uri this fetches arbitrary URLs. A value beginning with `|` would execute a shell command. The url ultimately comes from the embed_url request param. TopicRetriever restricts the host to embeddable_host, but Disqus import does not. Use URI.parse(url).open or an HTTP client instead.

findings.title: Feed item content may be nil, and String#scrub is unavailable on older Ruby
findings.body: `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError when an item has no content, which aborts the whole poll. Entries that only have a description would fail. `scrub` also requires Ruby 2.1+. The unused feed_key method is dead code.

findings.title: Non-atomic setnx plus expire
findings.body: If the process dies between setnx and expire, the key never expires. That URL is then throttled forever. Use `set` with ex and nx, or setex.

findings.title: Unrelated edit to an existing migration adds force: true
findings.body: Editing a historical migration to add `force: true` makes it drop the existing top_topics table (and its data) if the migration is re-run. Changes unrelated to this feature should not be made to old migrations.

findings.title: skip_validations now applies to all revisions
findings.body: `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` is a sensible extension, but the post_revisor change is untested. Also, update_post does not handle raw_html cook_method specially, so cooked is recomputed in before_save via cook, which depends on cook_method being preserved. This is subtle, and no test covers updating an existing embedded post's cooked.
